name: Bell-LaPadula access-control decisions and label lattice
identify_givens: A BLP system stated as: an ordered set of sensitivity levels (e.g. U < C < S < TS, written H = top secret > secret > confidential > unclassified), optionally a set of compartments (e.g. Alpha, Beta, Gamma), the label form L = (SL, C) with dominance L1 ⊑ L2 iff SL1 ≤ SL2 and C1 ⊆ C2, and concrete subject clearances fs/fc and object classifications fo (given as tables or bullet lists). Access modes read, write (implies read), append (write-only), and sometimes the state triple (b, f, H).
identify_target: Formally define no-read-up (ss-property: read iff fo(o) ⊑ fs(s)) and no-write-down (*-property: write iff fc(s) ⊑ fo(o)); then decide grant/deny for each listed (subject, object, mode) request and name the violated BLP rule when denied; possibly draw the label partial order (Hasse diagram over levels × compartment powerset) or construct example labels achieving a specified allowed/denied read/write combination.
strategy_name: Dominate-and-decide: formalize the two rules, then check dominance for each request

algorithm.detail: State the label order: for $L_1 = (SL_1, C_1)$ and $L_2 = (SL_2, C_2)$, $L_1 \sqsubseteq L_2$ iff $SL_1 \leq SL_2$ (linear level order) and $C_1 \subseteq C_2$ (compartment subset). If the problem has no compartments, dominance is just $SL_1 \leq SL_2$.

No read up (ss-property): subject $s$ may read object $o$ iff $f_o(o) \sqsubseteq f_s(s)$. No write down (*-property): $s$ may write $o$ iff $f_c(s) \sqsubseteq f_o(o)$. Write = read+write; append = write-only, and append is allowed exactly when $f_c(s) \sqsubseteq f_o(o)$ holds without requiring read.

Write out the concrete label of every subject and object from the tables, e.g. User 1: $(S, \{A, B\})$, File D: $(U, \{\})$. Track current clearance $f_c$ vs maximum clearance $f_s$ if both are given (access checks use the appropriate one as the problem states).

For each (subject, object, mode) triple: for read test $f_o(o) \sqsubseteq f_s(s)$; for write/append test $f_c(s) \sqsubseteq f_o(o)$. Evaluate the level comparison and the compartment subset separately; both must hold.

For each request state grant or deny plus the exact reason: which dominance holds or fails, and in case of denial name the violated rule (ss-property / no read up, or *-property / no write down). For incomparable labels (neither $L_1 \sqsubseteq L_2$ nor $L_2 \sqsubseteq L_1$), answer: neither read nor write.

If asked to draw the partial order, place level-compartment pairs as nodes with edges from $(SL, C)$ to the next higher level with the same compartments and to $(SL, C \cup \{x\})$ for each compartment $x \notin C$; the bottom is (lowest level, $\emptyset$), the top is (highest level, all compartments). If asked to construct example labels for a desired outcome, pick levels/compartments satisfying (or violating) the corresponding dominance.

variations.name: Compartments vs no compartments
variations.detail: The dasak18 instance (HT2018) explicitly drops compartments and the access matrix ('assume ds-property satisfied, no compartments') — dominance reduces to the linear level order, so incomparability never arises. The newer exam adds three compartments; there the trap is comparing only levels and forgetting $C_1 \subseteq C_2$: e.g. User 1 (S,{A,B}) vs File B (S,{G}) have equal levels but incomparable labels, so neither read nor write is allowed. Adapt step 4 to always check both components.

variations.name: Mode trap: append and write-implies-read
variations.detail: Some sittings distinguish write (implies read) from append (write-only). Carol (confidential) append to budget (secret) is allowed via the *-property even though she could not read the file — the trap is denying append because read would be denied. Conversely a write request must sometimes satisfy both rules if write implies read in the stated model.

variations.name: Max vs current clearance
variations.detail: When both $f_s$ (max) and $f_c$ (current) are tabulated (dasak18: Bob max secret, current confidential), using the wrong function flips verdicts — Bob's write to budget was denied with $f_c(Bob) \neq f_o(budget)$. Read the problem's convention for which function guards which property before deciding.

variations.name: Construction and lattice-drawing subtasks
variations.detail: Instead of (or besides) deciding requests, the exam asks to draw the Hasse diagram of the label lattice or to invent labels achieving a specified outcome (e.g. read allowed: $L_U = (TS, \{A\})$, $L_F = (S, \{A\})$; write allowed: $L_U = (S, \{A\})$, $L_F = (TS, \{A\})$). The algorithm adapts by running the dominance checks in reverse: choose compartments as subsets/supersets and levels ordered as the target requires.

example_problem: A defense organization uses BLP with levels U < C < S < TS and compartments Alpha (A), Beta (B), Gamma (G). User 1: (S, {A, B}); User 2: (C, {G}). File A: (TS, {A, B}); File B: (S, {G}); File C: (C, {A}); File D: (U, {}). First define no read up / no write down, then for each user decide with justification whether they can read or write each listed file (User 1: Files A, B, D; User 2: Files A, B, C).

example_steps.work: Dominance: $L_1 = (SL_1, C_1) \sqsubseteq L_2 = (SL_2, C_2)$ iff $SL_1 \leq SL_2$ and $C_1 \subseteq C_2$, with $C_i \subseteq \{A, B, G\}$.

No read up: U may read F iff $L_F \sqsubseteq L_U$. No write down: U may write F iff $L_U \sqsubseteq L_F$. Example labels: read allowed with $L_U = (TS, \{A\})$, $L_F = (S, \{A\})$; write allowed with $L_{U1} = (S, \{A\})$, $L_{F1} = (TS, \{A\})$.
Instantiate: User 1 $= (S, \{A,B\})$; User 2 $= (C, \{G\})$; File A $= (TS, \{A,B\})$; File B $= (S, \{G\})$; File C $= (C, \{A\})$; File D $= (U, \{\})$.

Summarize each verdict with its justification: allowed accesses cite the dominance that holds (e.g. *-property $L_{U2} \sqsubseteq L_{FB}$ for the write); denied accesses name the violated rule (no read up for User 1/File A read, no write down for User 1/File D write, both rules for the incomparable pairs).
